subject: Medford High School Building Project
overview: Host John Petrella interviewed Medford Public Schools Superintendent Dr. Suzanne B. Galusi regarding the ongoing Medford High School building project. Galusi outlined instructional goals, space programming considerations, facility conditions, and the preservation of community-facing programs.

items.title: Introduction
items.summary: Host John Petrella introduced Superintendent Dr. Suzanne B. Galusi to discuss plans for the high school and vocational facility.

items.title: Educational Outcomes and Instructional Vision
items.summary: Superintendent Galusi outlined the district's pre-K–12 instructional vision and described how a redesigned facility would better integrate Career Technical Education with academic classrooms to foster student collaboration and belonging.

items.title: Facility Design, Flexibility, and Adjacencies
items.summary: Galusi discussed the five design concepts under consideration ahead of a June 10 selection meeting, highlighting the need for ADA accessibility, flexible multi-use learning hubs, and intentional adjacencies between academic and vocational shops.

items.title: Project Investment and Space Allocation
items.summary: Galusi addressed space reduction reviews per MSBA guidelines, emphasizing priorities to protect instructional areas and vital community programs like municipal daycare and the Medford Family Network while reviewing shop-specific offices and central administration spaces.

items.title: Value Proposition and Cost of Inaction
items.summary: Galusi outlined the operational costs of maintaining the aging 1970 facility, including pool roof deterioration and HVAC issues, arguing that inaction compromises student learning environments and risks displacing critical civic programs.

items.title: Closing Remarks
items.summary: Petrella and Galusi concluded the interview, noting future updates will follow as the building committee advances design phases.
